Q: Can I use cache decorator to save result of any function call? A:

Is is possible to use it on other contexts, like for deterministic functions (that return the same result provided the same arguments)?

Yes, but this is only useful if the function is frequently called and the function body is more expensive than a dictionary lookup.

Should I avoid it if the function is non-deterministic?

Try out this code and see what it does:

import random

@functools.lru_cache
def die():
    print("Simulating a die throw")
    return random.randrange(1, 7)

for i in range(100):
    print(die())

I wonder what happens when the function takes no arguments

The function arguments are captured in a tuple, so it does something like:

if () not in self.cache:
    res = f()
    self.cache[()] = res
    return res
else:
    return self.cache[()]

So it works, but the dictionary will only ever have a single slot. Maybe useful for a quick-and-dirty singleton.

Q: TextBox is not editable inside ListViewItem ControlTemplate in WPF A:

I’ve run into something similar with custom TextBox templates. One thing I’d check is the ScrollViewer inside the ControlTemplate, especially whether making PART_ContentHost non-focusable is interfering with keyboard input. The binding itself looks fine, so the custom template seems like a likely place to investigate.

Q: Selenium (Chrome 136): "Failed to decrypt" errors with copied profile prevent use of existing login session A:

Why it fails: the "Failed to decrypt" flood is Chrome's app-bound encryption working as designed. Since Chrome 127 (tightened through 136), cookies and other profile secrets on Windows are encrypted by os_crypt with a key that is unwrapped by a broker service bound to that specific Chrome installation (the IElevator COM service validates the calling app). A profile copied into a different user-data-dir cannot unwrap that key, so every protected value throws os_crypt_win.cc "Failed to decrypt". Google cookies are among the protected values, which is why your AI Studio session is gone even though the files copied fine. Chrome added this specifically as an anti-cookie-theft measure, so the copy-the-profile strategy is dead for Google sessions on Chrome 136+. Nothing in your setup is wrong; the workaround itself is.

What still works:

1. Point Selenium at the original profile in place (no copy):

opts.add_argument(r"--user-data-dir=C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data")
opts.add_argument("--profile-directory=Default")

Every chrome.exe must be closed first ("user data directory is already in use" otherwise). Same machine, same Chrome install: the app-bound key unwraps fine and the Google session is intact. Tradeoffs: your daily browser has to be closed for every run, and the automated session runs with your real profile on the line.

2. Attaching over CDP is mostly gone for this case. Chrome 136 also disabled --remote-debugging-port for the default user-data-dir, so connecting via debuggerAddress against your real profile no longer works (non-default dirs only).

3. An extension inside the running browser sidesteps both restrictions: no profile copy, no relaunch, and the session never leaves the original profile. Disclosure: I built one (MIT, open source). chrome-bridge: a small Chrome extension plus a zero-dependency Node CLI; it reads pages as an accessibility tree and clicks by element refs, and anything that can run a shell command can drive it (call it from Python via subprocess). https://github.com/siropkin/chrome-bridge

One-line summary: after 136, copying the profile to reuse a Google session is no longer a workaround. Drive the original profile with Chrome closed, or drive the running browser through an extension.

Q: How can I install Pytorch in VS code on Windows? A:

Your python version is likely not supported yet

try

pip3 install --pre torch -f https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/cpu/torch_nightly.html

Q: Error during setup:di:compile - Incompatible argument type A:

I suppose $typeConfig is what you want to add into your own class. You need to pass all the variables into parent class besides setting $this->typeConfig.

Try this

public function __construct(
    \Magento\Backend\Block\Template\Context $context,
    \Magento\Backend\Model\Session\Quote $sessionQuote,
    \Magento\Sales\Model\AdminOrder\Create $orderCreate,
    PriceCurrencyInterface $priceCurrency,
    \Magento\Wishlist\Model\WishlistFactory $wishlistFactory,
    \Magento\GiftMessage\Model\Save $giftMessageSave,
    \Magento\Tax\Model\Config $taxConfig,
    \Magento\Tax\Helper\Data $taxData,
    \Magento\GiftMessage\Helper\Message $messageHelper,
    StockRegistryInterface $stockRegistry,
    StockStateInterface $stockState,
    array $data = [],
    \Magento\Catalog\Model\ProductTypes\ConfigInterface $typeConfig // your variable
) {
   $this->typeConfig = $typeConfig; // your variable
   parent::__construct(
              $context, 
              $sessionQuote, 
              $orderCreate, 
              $priceCurrency, 
              $wishlistFactory, 
              $giftMessageSave, 
              $taxConfig, 
              $taxData, 
              $messageHelper, 
              $stockRegistry, 
              $stockState, 
              $data
    );
}

Q: Is there UI to manage ASP.NET Identity users/roles compatible with ASP.NET 5? A:

If you want get all of roles and users with UI to manage asp.net Identity.

Try to make new blank asp.net MVC project. Make sure do not click Individual User Account. Then go to Package Manager Console and hit following query on console.

Install-Package Microsoft.AspNet.Identity.Samples -Version 2.2.0-alpha1

This package contains an asp.net MVC application which shows you how to use the features in asp.net Identity. Also compatible with asp.net. You should check default role and users once you connect database with ApplicationDbContext.
